title: WM-MT148-MergeRuntimeProofs
clause: Live end-to-end proofs: clean/conflict/patch/abort merge-back through the real APIs + negative proofs (no force-push, protected denied, dirty blocked) + Windows longpaths regression

scope.summary:
GOAL: Prove the whole WM Worktree merge-back family LIVE, end to end, exercising the real MT-141..147 APIs (not mocks of them) in a scratch git repo and real session worktrees, and lock the family's hard rules with executable NEGATIVE proofs. This MT ships NO new product behavior — it is the runtime acceptance surface that makes the family's guarantees externally verifiable and re-runnable by a no-context model.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New integration tests under src/backend/handshake_core/tests/ (a wm_merge_back_e2e suite) plus, where the conflict-resolution equivalence is proven through the UI bridge, a headless handshake_native integration test reusing the MT-143 bridge API. A small shared test-harness helper (scratch repo + real session worktree provisioning via MT-141) may be added under tests/ only. No src/ product code changes; if a proof cannot pass without a product change, that is a defect to route back to the owning MT (141..147), NOT patched here.

DETAILED SPEC — POSITIVE PROOFS (through the real APIs):
1. Clean merge (ff): provision a session branch (MT-141 ensure_session_worktree_allocation_with_mode SessionBranch), advance it ahead of target, MergeSession::begin with allow_fast_forward => MergeOutcome::CleanMerged{fast_forward:true}, target ref advances; then MT-147 reclaim_after_merge with DeleteOnReclaim => worktree removed + branch deleted + RECLAIMED emitted.
2. Clean merge (no-ff 3-way): divergent-but-non-conflicting edits => CleanMerged{fast_forward:false} with the attribution trailer; MT-145 governance emits Proposed+Approved+Executed audit rows + MT-161 FR kinds.
3. Conflict scenario resolved through the SAME bridge API the UI uses: overlapping edits => MergeOutcome::Conflicts; drive conflict_file_versions -> programmatic Accept choices through the MT-143 merge_conflict_bridge (the exact API MT-146's pane calls) -> resolve_conflict -> complete() => merge commit with resolved contents + trailers. This proves the governed-session path and the operator-UI path are ONE path.
4. Patch fallback (MT-144): from a DETACHED/legacy worktree (MT-141 DetachedHead compat mode) extract_session_patch_bundle => apply_session_patch_bundle onto target => Applied with commit count == bundle patch count; and a conflicting patch apply resolved through the SAME MT-143 bridge -> `git am --continue`.
5. Abort path: a conflicted MergeSession aborted (or dropped) => no MERGE_HEAD, target checkout pristine, target ref unchanged; MT-145 emits an Aborted audit row.

DETAILED SPEC — NEGATIVE PROOFS (the hard rules, proven by failure/denial):
6. Force-push impossibility: (a) static — assert ZERO force/push tokens across the family's command-constructing modules: `grep -rnE '(--force|--force-with-lease|\"-D\"|[^a-z]push[^a-z])' src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge_policy.rs` returns nothing; (b) runtime — assert no `git push` process is ever spawned during the entire e2e suite (the family is merge-back-LOCAL only; a push happens only if the operator explicitly configures publishing OUTSIDE this family) and that merge/patch command construction contains no force flag.
7. Protected-branch merge denied without approval: MT-145 ProtectedBranchPolicy marks the target protected; MergeSession::begin with NO MergeApprovalGrant => MergeOutcome::Blocked{TargetProtectedApprovalRequired}, NO merge commit, Proposed+Blocked audit rows; then WITH a valid operator grant => Executed. Proves the consent gate is real, not advisory.
8. Dirty-tree blocked: a dirty target checkout and (separately) a dirty source worktree each => MergeOutcome::Blocked{DirtyTargetTree|DirtySourceTree}, no MERGE_HEAD created, no partial merge.
9. Windows longpaths regression: create a tracked path deep enough to exceed the 260-char legacy limit under the session worktree, run the clean-merge and patch-apply flows, and assert they SUCCEED (core.longpaths=true is honored); additionally assert every git invocation the family constructs includes `-c core.longpaths=true` (scan the command-builder call sites / captured command lines).

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the MT-141..147 module surfaces (workspace_safety.rs session provisioning + reclaim, source_control_merge.rs engine, source_control_merge_policy.rs gate, merge_conflict_bridge.rs, MT-144 patch functions) so the tests call the REAL entry points.
2. Build the shared scratch-repo + real-session-worktree harness (temp dir, `git init`, seed commits, provision session worktrees via MT-141) under tests/.
3. Implement positive proofs 1-5 driving the real APIs; assert git-observable state (rev-parse, ls-files -u, MERGE_HEAD absence, worktree list) and MT-145 audit rows / FR events via a RecordingSwarmSink.
4. Implement negative proofs 6-9, including the static greps as proof targets and the runtime no-push / longpaths assertions.
5. Ensure the conflict proof (3) and the patch-conflict proof (4) both go through the MT-143 bridge API — the same API MT-146's pane calls — so UI/governed-session equivalence is demonstrated, not assumed.
6. Run the full suite; record measured output (pass/fail per scenario) and the grep proof-target results.

HARD RULES: this MT PROVES the family's rules, it does not re-implement or weaken them; NEVER force-push and NEVER auto-resolve inside the proofs (the conflict proofs resolve only via explicit bridge Accept choices); protected merges are exercised through the real MT-145 gate; git worktree CODE merge stays separate from CRDT document merging (no CRDT state in these proofs); every git call in the harness uses -c core.longpaths=true and holds SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK where it mutates worktrees.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml (dev-dependencies only, if a test needs one)
forbidden_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/** (proofs must not modify product code; a failing proof is a defect routed back to MT-141..147, never patched here)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/** (CRDT document merging is a separate domain)
acceptance_criteria: A live e2e suite provisions a scratch git repo and REAL session worktrees (MT-141) and drives the real MT-142/143/144/145/147 entry points — not reimplemented merge logic.

Positive: clean ff merge, clean no-ff 3-way merge (with attribution trailer), and a conflict resolved through the MT-143 bridge API all produce the expected git-observable commit + target-ref state, with MT-145 audit rows and MT-161 FR kinds recorded via a RecordingSwarmSink.

Positive: patch fallback (MT-144) from a DetachedHead legacy worktree applies onto target with commit count == bundle patch count, and a conflicting patch is resolved through the SAME MT-143 bridge -> `git am --continue`.
Positive: an aborted/dropped conflicted merge leaves no MERGE_HEAD, a pristine target checkout, and an unchanged target ref, with an Aborted audit row.

Negative (force-push impossibility): static grep across source_control_merge.rs + source_control_merge_policy.rs finds zero force/push tokens, AND the runtime suite spawns no `git push` and constructs no force flag.

Negative (protected denied): a protected target with no operator grant returns Blocked{TargetProtectedApprovalRequired} with no merge commit; the same merge with a valid grant Executes — proving the MT-145 consent gate is enforced, not advisory.
Negative (dirty blocked): dirty target and dirty source each return Blocked{DirtyTargetTree|DirtySourceTree} with no MERGE_HEAD and no partial merge.
Windows longpaths regression: a >260-char tracked path merges and patch-applies successfully, and every family git invocation is shown to include -c core.longpaths=true.
The conflict and patch-conflict proofs both resolve exclusively via explicit MT-143 bridge Accept choices (no auto-resolution), demonstrating operator-UI and governed-session equivalence.
code_surfaces: src/backend/handshake_core/tests/wm_merge_back_e2e.rs (NEW: scratch-repo + real-session-worktree harness driving the whole family)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/workspace_safety.rs (REUSE: MT-141 provisioning + MT-147 reclaim entry points)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/merge_conflict_bridge.rs (REUSE: MT-143 bridge API the conflict proofs drive)
expected_tests: e2e: clean ff merge -> CleanMerged{ff:true}, target advances, MT-147 reclaim removes worktree + deletes merged branch
e2e: no-ff 3-way -> CleanMerged{ff:false} + attribution trailer + Proposed/Approved/Executed audit rows
e2e: overlapping edits -> Conflicts -> resolved via MT-143 bridge Accept choices -> complete() commit with resolved contents
e2e: DetachedHead worktree -> patch bundle -> apply onto target (commit count == patch count); conflicting patch -> bridge -> am --continue
e2e: abort/drop conflicted merge -> no MERGE_HEAD, pristine checkout, unchanged ref, Aborted audit row
negative: protected target no grant -> Blocked{TargetProtectedApprovalRequired}; with grant -> Executed
negative: dirty target / dirty source -> Blocked{DirtyTargetTree|DirtySourceTree}, no MERGE_HEAD
negative: >260-char path merges + patch-applies OK; every git invocation carries -c core.longpaths=true; no git push spawned; static grep = zero force/push tokens
implementation_notes: These are proofs, not features: forbidden_paths block src/ edits precisely so a proof that fails becomes a defect ticket against the owning MT (141..147), never a quiet patch that hides the gap.

Drive the REAL entry points: import MT-141 provisioning, the MT-142 engine, the MT-143 bridge, the MT-144 patch functions, and the MT-145 gate directly; a proof that mocks the thing it claims to prove is worthless.

The conflict proof MUST use the MT-143 bridge API (the same one MT-146's pane calls) so the test demonstrates that the operator UI and the governed/programmatic resolution session are literally the same code path (the equivalence MT-143/146 asserted but deferred proving live).
no-push runtime proof: since std::process::Command spawns `git`, assert no invocation's args begin with `push`; combine with the static grep so both construction and execution are covered.

longpaths regression: on non-Windows CI the >260-char path still exercises the flag plumbing; the assertion that every command carries -c core.longpaths=true is the portable part and must pass on every platform.
Reclaim (MT-147) is included in the positive flow so the family is proven from provisioning through merge through resource reclaim in one arc, matching the real session lifecycle.
Keep the harness deterministic (fixed author/committer env, --no-gpg-sign already in the engine) so the proofs are reproducible by a no-context model.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless runtime-proof suite; the operator surface itself is proven in MT-146 (Argus). This MT's evidence is deterministic test output + git-observable state + grep proof targets, reconstructable without a UI (HBR-VIS-004).

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Proof-only MT: it ships no new user-facing behavior. The merge-back behaviors it verifies are documented by the manual updates in MT-141..147; this MT adds no manual entry of its own.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: The positive proofs assert MT-145 audit rows + MT-161 merge FR kinds and MT-147 RECLAIMED/CLEANUP-FAILED events via a RecordingSwarmSink, so the family's Flight-Recorder wiring is proven live, not assumed.
A test suite does not itself emit product diagnostics; it verifies the diagnostics the implementing MTs emit. Any test-harness failure surfaces through the normal cargo-test failure channel.
Deterministic bounded test processes; no long-lived runtime whose freeze/crash needs external liveness capture.

risk_if_missed: The family's guarantees stay claims: no force-push, protected-branch consent, dirty-tree blocking, UI/governed-session equivalence, and Windows longpaths safety are asserted in prose but never proven together at runtime, so a regression in any one ships silently and merge-back can corrupt or lose work.

risks: RISK-1: The proofs mock the very APIs they claim to verify (a fake merge engine / fake gate), so the suite is green while the real path is broken — proof theater.
RISK-2: The conflict proof resolves via a shortcut instead of the MT-143 bridge, so operator-UI vs governed-session equivalence is asserted but not actually exercised.
RISK-3: A proof silently patches product code (edits src/) to make itself pass, hiding a real defect in MT-141..147 instead of surfacing it.
RISK-4: The negative proofs are too weak — a grep that misses a force/push token, or a protected-denied test that never checks a merge commit was NOT created — passing without proving the rule.
RISK-5: The longpaths proof only runs on Windows and is skipped elsewhere, so the -c core.longpaths=true plumbing regresses undetected on the CI platform.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Tests import and call the real MT-141..147 entry points; a reviewer checklist item (and code_surfaces list) confirms no in-test reimplementation of merge/gate logic; assertions are on git-observable state, not on mock return values.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): The conflict and patch-conflict proofs call the exact MT-143 merge_conflict_bridge functions MT-146's pane calls; the test names and code_surfaces pin this, and the resolved-buffer-equals-committed assertion is shared with MT-146's CTRL-3.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): forbidden_paths block src/ edits; any proof that cannot pass without a product change is reported as a defect against the owning MT, not fixed here — stated as a hard rule in scope.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Negative proofs assert the ABSENCE of the forbidden outcome explicitly (no merge commit / no MERGE_HEAD / no push process) in addition to the typed Blocked reason; the force/push grep pattern covers --force, --force-with-lease, -D, and word-boundary push, and is a standalone proof target.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): The longpaths proof splits into a portable part (every git invocation carries -c core.longpaths=true — runs on all platforms) and the >260-char path exercise; the portable assertion must pass on the CI platform so the flag plumbing cannot regress undetected.

research_provenance.source: Verified current code across the family's grounding: wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 source_control.rs (status/diff/stage/commit/branch, NO merge — the gap MT-142 fills), workspace_safety.rs (session worktree provisioning + cleanup + SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK + -c core.longpaths=true, collect_merge_back_artifact ~331), swarm_orchestration/events.rs (RecordingSwarmSink + SwarmFrEventId table lines 33-109 for FR assertions), swarm_orchestration/worktree_vm_registry.rs (snapshot/teardown for MT-147 reclaim). The MT-141..147 contracts define the entry points this suite drives; the MT-143 bridge is the shared UI/governed-session resolution path. Field practice: end-to-end scratch-repo integration tests over the real CLI-git command layer (rather than libgit2 unit mocks) are the standard way to prove a merge subsystem's safety invariants, and negative/denial proofs (no force-push, protected-branch denial, dirty-tree block) are the field pattern for locking a merge tool's hard rules against regression.
corrections: This MT proves the operator/red-team hard rules of the whole family rather than re-implementing them: never force-push, no auto-resolution (bridge Accept choices only), protected-branch consent enforced by the real MT-145 gate, dirty-tree blocked, Windows longpaths honored.
Proof-only discipline: forbidden_paths block src/ so a failing proof is a defect against the owning MT, keeping the acceptance surface honest.

Git worktree CODE merge is exercised strictly separately from CRDT document merging (no CRDT state in these proofs); the conflict proofs demonstrate operator-UI and governed-session equivalence through the single MT-143 bridge API.
